reason: The iron-group core lacks fusion support, so gravity should drive its collapse.
expectation: The core will collapse, setting up the star’s explosion.

effect: The unsupported iron-group core is collapsing, producing neutrons and escaping neutrinos.
reaction: The formation of neutrons makes the collapse more concrete.
reason: The flood of neutrinos may help drive the explosion as the core collapses.
expectation: Neutrinos will contribute to an outward shock or explosion.

effect: Neutrino energy deposition has produced an outward shock that can interact with the star’s layers.
reaction: The qualification that this is one modeled route is useful.
reason: The outward shock should sweep through the onion of burning shells and scatter enriched material.
expectation: The shock will eject the star’s enriched layers.

effect: The shock has scattered the enriched layers, leaving the central remnant goal.
reaction: The distinction between nuclei made in the star and in the explosion is useful.
reason: The collapsing core should lead to the remnant, but its next partner is not clear.
expectation: Its available combinations should show how to find the neutron star.

effect: Inspecting the collapsing core revealed its sole partner and automatically formed a neutron star, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The contrast with a more massive remnant becoming a black hole was useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Combining the shock with the stellar layers connected the explosion to the dispersal of elements made both before and during it.

leastWorthwhile.text: The final inspection was useful, but applying gravity again to form the remnant was less intuitive than the earlier combinations.

surprise.text: The account qualified neutrino-driven shock revival as one modeled route rather than the fate of every massive star.

arbitrary.text: Using gravity without fusion support a second time to produce a neutron star felt somewhat opaque; the inspection supplied the partner rather than explaining why it was needed.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to follow the enriched ejecta toward the formation of rock and water, especially given the chapter’s careful distinctions between possible stellar outcomes.
